name: Battle of Yarmouk

sides.name: Rashidun Caliphate
sides.commander: Khalid ibn al-Walid, Abu Ubaidah ibn al-Jarrah
sides.strength: Approximately 25,000 to 40,000 mounted and foot Arab troops

sides.name: Byzantine Empire
sides.strength: Approximately 80,000 to 100,000 Byzantine, Armenian, and Christian Arab auxiliaries
sides.casualties: Estimates range from 45,000 to 70,000 killed or scattered

summary: Khalid ibn al-Walid concentrated his cavalry against a Byzantine army drawn up along the Yarmouk gorge, a system of ravines feeding the Yarmouk River near the modern borders of Jordan, Israel, and Syria. Over six days the Arabs pressed both wings, exploited a sandstorm and a desertion among the Christian Arab Ghassanid auxiliaries, then broke the Byzantine right and drove the army into the ravines on the sixth day. The remnant could not reach Damascus.
significance: Yarmouk ended Byzantine rule over the Levant. Within four years the Arabs took Damascus, Antioch, Jerusalem, and Alexandria. The intellectual and trade centers of the eastern Roman world transferred to a new Arab Muslim civilization, and the religious geography of the Mediterranean was reset for fourteen centuries.
